pages.text: A $(item)Descriptive Book$() creates and links to an Age the first time you use it. A $(item)Linking Book$() records the exact place where it was written. Descriptive books define worlds. Linking books define destinations.

On first use, a descriptive book reads its pages, claims its chosen name, creates the dimension, and places you at a sanitized arrival point. Mystcraft now checks that arrival so you are far less likely to appear inside solid terrain.
If you die in an Age without a personal spawn set, you respawn back into that Age. Unsafe Ages can still strand you, so a prepared explorer keeps a spare linking book or a crystal portal route home.

Sacrificed Ages are different. Survival and adventure players are expelled from them. Linking books fail with unreadable, running ink. Creative and spectator players can still inspect the hollow remains, but for ordinary travel that world is dead.
